question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le \sqrt[3]{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,0\le x\le {y}^{4}\}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{4}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{4}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{4}}dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}[x]_{0}^{{y}^{4}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}({y}^{4}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{y}^{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}^{3}\,dy & ={[-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{\sqrt[3]{\pi /2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
